conflict_topics: ventilation responsibility / standing rule for extractor use
window opening vs. Agent C's drying rack (risk of wetting clothes)
who may move Agent C's drying rack
dialogue_quality_notes: Agents used concise, contextual turns and acted on proposals (Agent B turned on extractor, Agent A released stove).
Positions were restated several times early on (A's refusal to accept a rule), but this repetition was relevant rather than needless.
Agent C remained mostly silent and their practical constraint (laundry risk) was stated in the setting but not actively negotiated.
Resolution was produced by a concrete concession (A accepted others turning on extractor) and enacted actions (stove release, B taking stove).
evaluation.final_reason: Particular disputes were settled: Agent A accepted that others may turn on the extractor and subsequently released the stove (stove access transferred). However, the related issue about moving Agent C's drying rack if the window were to be opened was never addressed and remains unconfirmed, so the situation is only partially resolved.
position_change_notes: Agent A shifted position: initially refused any rule making the cook always handle ventilation, then accepted that others may turn on the extractor while someone cooks (softening/concession).
Agent B moved from insisting the cook should ventilate to accepting a standing practice that others may turn on the extractor (compromise).
Agent D consistently requested stove access but did not change position; their need was accommodated once the stove was released.
Agent C did not articulate a negotiated position about moving the drying rack; their practical vulnerability (wet laundry) remained unaddressed.

round_scores.evidence: Agent A refused to accept a standing rule making the cook handle ventilation; Agent B demanded the cook ventilate and proposed a standing rule; Agent B turned the extractor on. Multiple incompatible claims about ventilation responsibility and stove access remained.

Agent A reiterated refusal to accept a rule and requested more cooking time; Agent B repeated the proposal that others may turn on the extractor while someone cooks. The core disagreement about a standing ventilation rule persisted.

Agent A conceded that others may turn on the extractor while someone is cooking; Agent B declared that they will treat that as the standing rule. Immediate stove timing still in play (one minute). The main ventilation-rule dispute was narrowed/resolved, leaving minor remaining issues (e.g., window/drying-rack risk).

Agent A released the stove as promised and Agent B took the stove. The previously contested stove-access timing and the extractor-use rule were implemented, removing the active substantive disputes recorded earlier.
Agent D asked how much longer; Agent B answered 'five minutes.' No substantive disagreement was expressed.
Agent D repeated requests for the stove; no new opposing claim or refusal appeared and no substantive conflict was reintroduced.

substantive_insights: The core tension was between a norm that the cook should manage ventilation and the practical constraint that opening the window would harm Agent C's drying laundry.
A low-friction operational rule (others may turn on extractor) resolved most of the odor-versus-effort dispute without requiring anyone to move the drying rack.

Immediate practical actions (turning on extractor, releasing stove) were effective at de-escalating the active conflict even though some edge-case responsibilities (moving the rack) were not negotiated.

normalizations: Removed resolution_round 4 because the final status is partially_resolved.
